1.0·L1 + 0.5·gradient + 0.2·(1 − SSIM)

the only term that does

weighted Dice + weighted cross-entropy

target is a THRESHOLD of the phase target

accuracy varied ±9.5 pts across 3 identical runs
MEASUREMENT — constrain in the units reported
L_cIPP per-cell integrated phase
★ THE HYPOTHESIS w = 0.1 → 0.299
V̂ᵢ = Σ_{p∈Ωᵢ} M̂(p)·φ̂(p)
L = mean_i |V̂ᵢ − Vᵢ| / (|Vᵢ| + ε)
domains Ωᵢ from the REFERENCE labelling — fixed,
so the term cannot be gamed by moving the mask

SUPERSEDED — scores 0.0000 on a ±20% pair

REDUNDANT — same ratio as L_PV, smooth-L1 shape
L_area projected area w = 0 in v2
consider restoring — area is a reported endpoint
PHYSICS — couple the outputs / read the sensor
L_fwd forward-model consistency w = 0
propagate φ̂ to the sensor, fit 6 radiometric
coefficients, compare with the RAW hologram
the ONLY term that reads the measurement
MEASURED: blind near the truth — margin +0.0002
and win rate 0.50 (chance) for a 10% phase rescale
→ rescoped in exp. D to supervise AMPLITUDE only
L_PMC phase–mask contrast w = 0
INERT — gap 1.370 rad vs 0.1 margin (13.7×)
logged EXACTLY 0.00000 in every v1 run
L_BGA boundary-gradient align. w = 0.05 in C
an ABLATION, not an assumption — established on
RBCs; these cells have thin lamellipodia
The foreground gate — why it exists
All measurement/coupling terms are RELATIVE errors, so they divide by the reference integral of the crop. A 512-px crop catching a sliver of one cell

divides by a near-zero reference and produces a spike that dominates the epoch. Crops with fewer than 512 foreground pixels (≈ one cell) are excluded. L_fwd is deliberately NOT gated: a crop without cells must still be consistent with the hologram it came from.
Why weighting matters at all
L_φ is in radians; L_seg is dimensionless in [0,2]; L_cIPP is a dimensionless relative error. Multiplying by a weight is the ONLY thing that puts them on a

comparable footing. A weight wrong by an order of magnitude means the constraint is either ignored or dominant — which is why the weight must be set from a MEASURED gradient ratio (0.299), not from a round number (0.1).
